title: OctoMap: an efficient probabilistic 3D mapping framework based on octrees
summary: Peer-reviewed (Autonomous Robots). Describes the octree occupancy map with log-odds updates, clamping for fast change, and explicit separation of free, occupied and unknown cells. Evaluates memory and update cost on large indoor and outdoor scans.
key_takeaways: Unknown is a separate state, not free
Clamping log-odds keeps the map responsive to change
Per-ray insertion cost grows with resolution and range

title: Voxblox: Incremental 3D Euclidean Signed Distance Fields for On-Board MAV Planning
summary: Preprint on arXiv; published at IROS 2017. Builds an ESDF incrementally from a TSDF so a CPU-only MAV can keep distance and gradient to obstacles up to date for trajectory optimisation.
key_takeaways: ESDF from TSDF is cheaper than from raw occupancy
Gradient-based planners need distance plus gradient, not just occupied or free
Runs on CPU at MAV scale

title: UFOMap: An Efficient Probabilistic 3D Mapping Framework That Embraces the Unknown
summary: Peer-reviewed (IEEE RA-L 2020, doi 10.1109/LRA.2020.3013861); arXiv copy linked. Extends octree mapping with an explicit unknown state and indicators per node so planners can ask whether a region is entirely known-free in one query.
key_takeaways: Explicit unknown enables safe 'known-free only' collision checks
Faster than OctoMap in the reported benchmarks
Built for planning and exploration queries

title: Efficient volumetric mapping of multi-scale environments using wavelet-based compression
summary: Peer-reviewed (RSS 2023). Stores occupancy as Haar wavelet coefficients in an octree, giving multi-resolution queries and good handling of thin structures at long range with low memory.
key_takeaways: Multi-resolution map without separate pyramids
Designed and tested for CPU-only systems
Thin obstacles survive better than in coarse fixed grids

title: nvblox: GPU-Accelerated Incremental Signed Distance Field Mapping
summary: Preprint on arXiv. Moves TSDF and ESDF integration onto the GPU and reports large speedups over CPU voxblox, targeting Jetson-class robots with RGB-D cameras.
key_takeaways: Same TSDF to ESDF pipeline as voxblox, on CUDA
Needs an NVIDIA GPU: no Apple Silicon path
Fits a Jetson companion with a depth camera

title: FASTER: Fast and Safe Trajectory Planner for Navigation in Unknown Environments
summary: Peer-reviewed (IEEE T-RO, doi 10.1109/TRO.2021.3100142); arXiv copy linked. Plans two trajectories each cycle: a fast one through known and unknown space, and a safe backup that stops inside known free space. Only the prefix up to the backup branch point is committed.
key_takeaways: Safety = always holding a stop trajectory in known free space
Optimism about unknown space is fine if it is never committed
Corridors from JPS + convex decomposition keep the problem an MIQP

title: Bubble Planner: Planning High-speed Smooth Quadrotor Trajectories using Receding Corridors
summary: Preprint on arXiv (authors list it as IROS 2022, not checked here). Builds a corridor of free-space spheres directly from a point cloud using a KD-tree, then optimises a smooth trajectory through it with a receding horizon. No official code release was found; third-party reproductions exist.
key_takeaways: Sphere corridors skip building a voxel map
Receding corridor gives high speed with modest compute
Only third-party code exists, so treat any repo as unvalidated

title: Integrated Planning and Control for Quadrotor Navigation in Presence of Suddenly Appearing Objects and Disturbances
summary: Peer-reviewed (IEEE RA-L). A light front end builds a safe flight corridor and a 100 Hz linear MPC on jerk with corridor constraints drives the vehicle, converting the output to body rates and thrust through differential flatness.
key_takeaways: Folding planning into a fast MPC loop reacts to sudden obstacles
Corridor half-planes become linear MPC constraints
Also rejects disturbances that break plan-then-track pipelines

title: Safety-assured high-speed navigation for MAVs
summary: Peer-reviewed (Science Robotics). LiDAR MAV planner that plans on point clouds and keeps an exploratory trajectory plus a backup trajectory in known free space each cycle. Reports far fewer failures than baselines and real flights above 20 m/s through clutter.
key_takeaways: Backup trajectory in known free space is the core safety mechanism
Planning directly on point clouds avoids map latency
Hardware: 3D LiDAR, high thrust-to-weight airframe

title: Swarm of micro flying robots in the wild
summary: Peer-reviewed (Science Robotics). The EGO-Planner-v2 paper: palm-sized drones fly through forest with onboard depth, a gradient-based local planner on a MINCO trajectory representation, and swarm coordination.
key_takeaways: ESDF-free gradient planning works on tiny compute
Depth camera + VIO is enough for forest-scale clutter
Same planner scales from one drone to a swarm

title: Planning Dynamically Feasible Trajectories for Quadrotors Using Safe Flight Corridors in 3-D Complex Environments
summary: Peer-reviewed (IEEE RA-L). Defines the safe flight corridor pipeline: 3D JPS path, convex polytopes grown around it, then a QP for a polynomial trajectory constrained to stay in the polytopes.
key_takeaways: Grid search => convex corridor => QP is a solid, explainable pipeline
Corridors make collision constraints linear
3D JPS keeps the front end fast

title: Search-based motion planning for quadrotors using linear quadratic minimum time control
summary: Peer-reviewed (IROS 2017). Kinodynamic graph search over short motion primitives with a cost that trades time against control effort, producing dynamically feasible trajectories directly.
key_takeaways: Search over primitives instead of grid cells gives feasible output
Cost to go is a minimum-time plus effort heuristic
Slower than geometric search in high dimensions

title: Online Graph Pruning for Pathfinding On Grid Maps
summary: Peer-reviewed (AAAI 2011). Introduces Jump Point Search: on uniform-cost grids, symmetric paths are pruned so A* expands only jump points, keeping optimality with far fewer expansions.
key_takeaways: Same optimal path as A* on uniform grids
Large speedups on open maps, smaller in cluttered ones
Needs uniform cost; clearance-weighted grids break the assumption

title: Sampling-based Algorithms for Optimal Motion Planning
summary: Peer-reviewed (IJRR 2011); arXiv copy linked. Introduces RRT* and PRM*, proving asymptotic optimality and showing that plain RRT converges to a suboptimal path.
key_takeaways: RRT* rewires to converge toward the optimal path
Plain RRT paths are feasible but jagged and long
Narrow passages remain hard for any uniform sampler

title: Probabilistic roadmaps for path planning in high-dimensional configuration spaces
summary: Peer-reviewed (IEEE Transactions on Robotics and Automation). Defines the probabilistic roadmap: sample free configurations, connect neighbours with a local planner, then answer queries with graph search.
key_takeaways: Build once, query many times: suits a static known close area
Coverage of narrow passages depends on sampling density
Local planner choice decides roadmap quality

title: Path Planning for Autonomous Vehicles in Unknown Semi-structured Environments
summary: Peer-reviewed (IJRR). The Hybrid A* paper from the DARPA Urban Challenge: A* over a discretised grid where each node keeps a continuous state reached by kinematically feasible motions, followed by numerical smoothing.
key_takeaways: Grid for pruning, continuous state for feasibility
Built for curvature-limited ground vehicles
For multirotors, kinodynamic search with motion primitives is the analogue

title: Real-Time Obstacle Avoidance for Manipulators and Mobile Robots
summary: Peer-reviewed (IJRR). The artificial potential field method: an attractive field toward the goal and repulsive fields around obstacles, with the robot following the negative gradient.
key_takeaways: Cheap, reactive, a few lines of code
Local minima and oscillation in narrow gaps are built in
Good as a baseline or a last-resort safety layer, not a planner

title: Potential field methods and their inherent limitations for mobile robot navigation
summary: Peer-reviewed (ICRA 1991). Lists the structural failures of potential fields: trap situations from local minima, no passage between closely spaced obstacles, oscillation near obstacles and in narrow passages.
key_takeaways: Local minima traps are inherent, not a tuning problem
Closely spaced obstacles can block a gap the robot fits through
Useful citation for why a global planner is needed

title: VFH+: reliable obstacle avoidance for fast mobile robots
summary: Peer-reviewed (ICRA 1998). Builds a polar histogram of obstacle density around the robot, enlarges obstacles by the robot radius and picks a free direction close to the goal heading, with hysteresis to stop flicker.
key_takeaways: Sector histogram from range data, no map needed
Robot-size enlargement and hysteresis fix the original VFH
Still a local method: dead ends need a global planner

title: Collision Prevention (PX4 User Guide)
summary: Docs. PX4's built-in collision prevention for multicopters in acceleration-based Position mode. It limits velocity toward obstacles seen by range sensors or OBSTACLE_DISTANCE MAVLink messages and can bend the commanded direction by up to CP_GUIDE_ANG. It does not plan a route.
key_takeaways: Position mode only, not Mission or Offboard
Directions without sensor data are blocked by default (CP_GO_NO_DATA = 0)
Missing range data for 0.5 s zeroes xy motion, 5 s triggers Hold

title: Path Planning Interface (PX4 User Guide, marked removed)
summary: Docs. The page for the old companion-computer obstacle avoidance interface (PX4-Avoidance, COM_OBS_AVOID). The main branch marks it removed; the v1.16 page says it is unsupported and should not be used in any version.
key_takeaways: PX4 no longer ships an onboard path-planning hook for avoidance
Companion planners now drive PX4 through Offboard or ROS 2 external modes
PX4-Avoidance repo is archived

title: Object Avoidance with BendyRuler (ArduPilot Copter docs)
summary: Docs. ArduPilot's onboard local avoidance for Copter and Rover in Auto, Guided and RTL. It probes candidate bearings up to OA_BR_LOOKAHEAD ahead against an object database fed by proximity sensors and fences, keeping OA_MARGIN_MAX clearance. Type 1 is horizontal only, type 2 also searches up and down.
key_takeaways: Works in Guided, so a companion can send goals and let BendyRuler dodge
Object database ages out obstacles after OA_DB_EXPIRE
Local method: no guarantee in dead ends

title: Object Avoidance with Dijkstra's (ArduPilot Copter docs)
summary: Docs. Onboard global path planning around polygon fences and stay-out zones in Auto, Guided (with GUID_OPTIONS bit 6) and RTL. It does not use proximity-sensor obstacles; a separate mode combines it with BendyRuler for that.
key_takeaways: Known static obstacles can be entered as stay-out polygons and avoided with zero companion code
No sensed-obstacle avoidance on its own
Spline waypoints are not supported
